mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to move a single-wide mobile home in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical full-service single-wide move within 50 miles of San Antonio costs $4,000 to $6,000, with a market median near $5,500. This includes skirting removal, utility disconnect, transport, setup (blocking, leveling, anchoring to HUD Wind Zone I standards), and basic utility reconnection. Transport-only local moves can run as low as $1,500 to $2,500 when setup is excluded. Mandatory costs include a $40 TxDMV manufactured housing single-trip permit, a $75 TDHCA installation reporting fee, and city permits. Most standard single-wides are under 16 feet wide, so no escort vehicle is required under Texas manufactured housing rules.

mainEntity.name: What is the average cost to move a double-wide mobile home in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full-service double-wide moves in San Antonio typically cost $10,000 to $14,000 for local moves under 50 miles, with a market median around $12,000. Double-wides must be split into two sections for transport, each requiring its own TxDMV permit ($80 total for two sections) and tow vehicle. The TDHCA installation reporting fee is $100 for two sections. Marriage-line reassembly at the destination adds $1,000 to $3,000. San Antonio city code requires permanent foundation placement and removal of wheels and axles at the destination.

mainEntity.name: Does distance affect mobile home moving costs in Texas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Distance is one of the biggest cost drivers. Local moves under 50 miles are often flat-rate, while longer moves shift to per-mile pricing at $4.00 to $5.50 per mile for the tow vehicle per section, plus $1.50 to $3.50 per mile for escort vehicles when required. The TxDMV permit fee remains a flat $40 per section regardless of distance. Interstate moves to Louisiana add $10 per trip LaDOTD permit, New Mexico adds $25, and Oklahoma adds $40. Per-mile rates decline as distance increases because fixed mobilization costs are spread over more miles.

mainEntity.name: What is the cheapest time of year to move a mobile home in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: January is the cheapest month for manufactured home transport in San Antonio, with pricing roughly 18% below the annual average. November through February generally offers the lowest rates due to reduced demand, shorter daylight windows, and fewer competing moves. The most expensive month is July at roughly 20% above baseline, when JBSA military PCS demand peaks, daylight hours are longest, and hurricane season diverts transporter capacity. Mid-week moves during off-peak months represent the lowest-cost scheduling window.

mainEntity.name: Are there hidden costs when moving a mobile home in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Common hidden costs in San Antonio include skirting removal and reinstallation ($900 to $2,400 for a single-wide), axle and tire rental ($1,000 to $2,000 for older homes), CPS Energy disconnect and reconnect fees ($53 to $600+ depending on scope), and SAWS deposits ($100). The biggest hidden cost risks are SAWS impact fees ($7,343 to $11,528) for new water and sewer connections on raw land, and foundation complications from Bexar County's expansive Houston Black clay soil or Hill Country limestone, which can add $4,000 to $40,000 in engineered foundation work. Sites on the Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone require TCEQ compliance costing $10,000 to $30,000+.

mainEntity.name: What permits are required to move a mobile home in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moving a manufactured home in San Antonio requires a TxDMV single-trip manufactured housing permit ($40 per section) filed through TxPROS, a TDHCA installation reporting fee ($75 for single-section, plus $25 per additional section), and local permits. Within City of San Antonio limits, a manufactured home installation permit is required through Development Services. The installer must hold an active TDHCA installer license with a $25,000 surety bond. Transport is restricted to daylight hours only and prohibited on six national holidays. Most standard single-wide sections under 16 feet wide require no escort vehicle under Texas rules.

mainEntity.name: How do I verify a mobile home mover in San Antonio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Verify a San Antonio transporter in four steps. First, check their TDHCA installer license at mhweb.tdhca.state.tx.us confirming Active status and a $25,000 bond. Second, pull their FMCSA SAFER Company Snapshot at safer.fmcsa.dot.gov to confirm their USDOT number shows Active with no out-of-service orders. Third, confirm they will obtain a TxDMV manufactured housing permit for your specific route through TxPROS. Fourth, request a Certificate of Insurance showing commercial auto liability (minimum $300,000 combined single limit per Texas law) and cargo coverage appropriate to your home's value. Red flags include an inactive USDOT record, inability to provide a TDHCA license number, or requests for full payment upfront.

mainEntity.name: What wind zone is San Antonio in for manufactured home installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bexar County and the San Antonio metro are classified as HUD Wind Zone I under 24 CFR 3280.305. Only 15 coastal Texas counties are designated Wind Zone II. Wind Zone I requires standard diagonal tie-down anchoring rated for 70 mph fastest-mile wind speed. A home's data plate wind rating must be compatible with the installation location. A Wind Zone I home cannot be installed in a Wind Zone II coastal county. Standard Wind Zone I anchoring costs $1,000 to $2,500 for a single-wide and $1,500 to $3,500 for a double-wide, though caliche or limestone substrate in the Hill Country may require cross-drive rock anchors at additional cost.
